name: Nitish V. Thakor
title: Professor of Biomedical Engineering, Electrical and Computer Engineering, and Neurology
department: Biomedical Engineering; Electrical and Computer Engineering; Neurology; Neuroengineering & Biomedical Instrumentation Lab
fitReason: Relevant computational work in tactile feature encoding, learned sensory discrimination and myoelectric prosthesis control. The current JHU faculty directory verifies the three professor titles, and the lab roster and 2025 university report independently connect the hand study to his supervised JHU doctoral work. His lab also reports an NUS appointment, so Baltimore availability requires confirmation.

physicalEvidence.summary: The fully inspected March 2025 Science Advances study demonstrates a hybrid pneumatic hand mounted on an actual UR5 and an able-bodied bypass-prosthesis demonstration: Myo Armband EMG classification sends hand positions to an Arduino for pneumatic actuation. Separate tactile perception uses Izhikevich spike encoding and a linear SVM on robot-collected signals, assessed by repeated four-fold cross-validation over 26 texture plates and 15 objects. The reported 99.69% is object classification accuracy, not grasp success. Learned tactile outputs are not shown closing the grasp-control loop; the paper explicitly leaves a sensory-feedback closed-loop prosthesis to future work. It was submitted July 30, 2024, so 2025 publication does not establish new 2025 hardware execution. This is an early prototype, not an amputee clinical trial or autonomous dexterous manipulation policy.

shortVisit.summary: The current lab roster includes JHU graduate and undergraduate researchers, master’s alumni and a historical visiting doctoral researcher. No lab-specific invitation for outside-master short visits, an eight-week summer 2027 placement, remote participation or funding was verified. The lab training program is explicitly for JHU BME PhD trainees.

scoreReasons.fit: Substantive learned tactile discrimination and EMG-based assistive robot control, with strong neuroengineering rather than general robot foundation-model emphasis.
scoreReasons.physical: Actual classified-EMG hand actuation is verified; conservative cap for pre-July-2024 execution and separation from offline tactile classification.
scoreReasons.shortVisit: No applicable outside-master visitor invitation verified.
scoreReasons.freshness: Current faculty and lab roster, 2026 activity and recent published research verified; older hardware chronology remains explicit.
